papers.title: Random Forest-Based Early Warning System for Student Dropout Using Behavioral Data
papers.objective: This paper addresses the development of a Random Forest-based early warning system for student dropout utilizing behavioral data. papers.abstract: This paper addresses the development of a Random Forest-based early warning system for student dropout utilizing behavioral data. Student dropout is a significant issue in educational institutions, impacting student success and institutional effectiveness. Current research in the field faces challenges in accurately predicting dropout risks due to the complexity and diversity of student behaviors. To tackle this issue, this study proposes an innovative approach that leverages Random Forest algorithm to analyze diverse behavioral data and effectively identify students at risk of dropping out. The system's design and implementation, incorporating machine learning techniques, offer a more accurate and efficient method for early identification of dropout risks, facilitating timely interventions to support student retention and success in academic settings.
papers.dataset: Behavioral data (synthetic dataset used for case study)
papers.algorithms: Random Forest, Logistic Regression
papers.main_findings: Random Forest achieved perfect accuracy (1.0) in the case study, significantly outperforming Logistic Regression (0.8 accuracy). The ensemble nature of Random Forests enables effective modeling of multifaceted relationships among academic performance, socio-economic status, and psychological variables.
papers.limitations: Evaluated on synthetic dataset rather than real institutional cohort
papers.research_gaps: Single-institution/synthetic scope or missing end-to-end EWS deployment in the brief
papers.relevance_type: Directly Related to Student Dropout Prediction
papers.eduguard_relevance: Enhanced Random Forest hyperparameter ensemble tuning with class weighting and bootstrap sampling.

papers.title: The Machine Learning-Based Dropout Early Warning System for Improving the Performance of Dropout Prediction
papers.objective: A dropout early warning system enables schools to preemptively identify students who are at risk of dropping out of school, to promptly react to them, and eventually to help potential dropout students to continue their learning for a better future. However, the inherent class imbalance between dropout and non-dropout s...
papers.abstract: A dropout early warning system enables schools to preemptively identify students who are at risk of dropping out of school, to promptly react to them, and eventually to help potential dropout students to continue their learning for a better future. However, the inherent class imbalance between dropout and non-dropout students could pose difficulty in building accurate predictive modeling for a dropout early warning system. The present study aimed to improve the performance of a dropout early warning system: (a) by addressing the class imbalance issue using the synthetic minority oversampling techniques (SMOTE) and the ensemble methods in machine learning; and (b) by evaluating the trained classifiers with both receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and precision-recall (PR) curves.
papers.dataset: National Education Information System (NEIS) - South Korea, 165,715 high school students
papers.algorithms: Random Forest, Boosted Decision Tree, Random Forest with SMOTE, Boosted Decision Tree with SMOTE
papers.class_imbalance: SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique); Class weighting / balanced variants; Random oversampling
papers.evaluation_metrics: Accuracy, AUC, PR-AUC, Precision, Recall, ROC, PR curves
papers.main_findings: Boosted Decision Tree showed the optimal performance with AUC of 0.991 on ROC curves and 0.898 on PR curves. PR curves were more informative than ROC curves for imbalanced datasets. Class imbalance handling through SMOTE significantly improved model performance.
papers.limitations: Not explicitly detailed in the 2-page PDF brief
papers.research_gaps: Single-institution/synthetic scope or missing end-to-end EWS deployment in the brief
papers.relevance_type: Directly Related to Student Dropout Prediction
papers.eduguard_relevance: Implementation of SMOTE oversampling pipeline combined with dual ROC and Precision-Recall (PR) curve evaluations.

papers.title: Application of Machine Learning in Higher Education and Academic Management as an Early Warning and Intervention System for Student Academic Learning
papers.objective: This study critically examines the application of machine learning technologies in higher education and academic management, with particular emphasis on their use as early warning and intervention systems for identifying students at risk of academic dropout. Employing a case study approach, the research focuses on a Ch...
papers.abstract: This study critically examines the application of machine learning technologies in higher education and academic management, with particular emphasis on their use as early warning and intervention systems for identifying students at risk of academic dropout. Employing a case study approach, the research focuses on a Chinese public-sector university recognised as a pioneer in the adoption of digital learning technologies and learning management systems (LMS). The empirical analysis is based on observational data and academic records of 141 undergraduate (BS) students enrolled across multiple programmes and disciplines. The results indicate that approximately 17% of the analysed students were classified as at risk of dropout.
papers.dataset: Chinese public-sector university data, 141 undergraduate students (2021-2024)
papers.feature_engineering: LMS/VLE behavioral engagement indicators (login frequency, inactivity, assignment submission)
papers.algorithms: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost
papers.evaluation_metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, AUC, F1-score
papers.main_findings: XGBoost emerged as the most effective model with 88% accuracy, 81% precision, 85% recall, 83% F1-score, and 92% AUC. Key behavioral factors included assignment submission timeliness, attendance rates, LMS login frequency, and completed credit hours. Counselling and tutoring strategies resulted in 86% GPA improvement for high-risk students.
papers.limitations: Small sample size (141 undergraduate students)
papers.research_gaps: Single-institution/synthetic scope or missing end-to-end EWS deployment in the brief
papers.relevance_type: Directly Related to Student Dropout Prediction
papers.eduguard_relevance: XGBoost behavioral modeling, composite engagement metrics, and GPA-recovery intervention protocols.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Early Warning for Student Dropout: Evidence from LMS Behavioral Engagement Patterns in Online Higher Education
papers.authors: Rhezwan Dhaifullah Romdhoni, Nuur Wachid Abdul Majid, Anggita Fitri Permatasari
papers.objective: Student dropout in online higher education remains critically high, far exceeding face-to-face rates, yet declining behavioral activity in Learning Management Systems (LMS) offers key signals for early intervention. To identify robust predictors and model suitability for Early Warning Systems (EWS), this study presents...
papers.abstract: Student dropout in online higher education remains critically high, far exceeding face-to-face rates, yet declining behavioral activity in Learning Management Systems (LMS) offers key signals for early intervention. To identify robust predictors and model suitability for Early Warning Systems (EWS), this study presents a comparative analysis of machine learning for dropout prediction using clickstream data from the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), covering 32,593 students across seven undergraduate modules. Three supervised algorithms-Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)-were trained on 13 engineered features combining behavioral and demographic attributes from the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE), with Recall prioritized to minimize missed at-risk students.
papers.dataset: Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), 32,593 students
papers.feature_engineering: 13 engineered VLE behavioral & demographic features (incl. Activity Span); LMS/VLE behavioral engagement indicators (login frequency, inactivity, assignment submission)
papers.algorithms: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM)
papers.main_findings: All models achieved AUC-ROC > 0.93. SVM provided the highest EWS fit with recall of 0.903, missing only 196 of 2,031 withdrawals (9.7%). Random Forest attained the best overall accuracy (0.866) and AUC-ROC (0.940). VLE behavior accounted for 85.0% of predictive power, with Activity Span emerging as the dominant predictor at 41.3%.
papers.limitations: Not explicitly detailed in the 2-page PDF brief
papers.research_gaps: Single-institution/synthetic scope or missing end-to-end EWS deployment in the brief
papers.relevance_type: Directly Related to Student Dropout Prediction
papers.eduguard_relevance: Activity Span feature engineering, SVM classifier addition, and recall-optimized threshold calibration.

papers.abstract: Student dropout remains a major challenge in asynchronous online learning due to limited direct interaction and the difficulty of identifying disengaged learners at an early stage. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a Learning Analytics-Based Early Warning System for predicting student dropout risk by integrating behavioral learning analytics, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence. Behavioral data were collected from a Learning Management System, including login frequency, learning inactivity, learning resource utilization, assignment submission, discussion participation, and other engagement indicators.
papers.feature_engineering: LMS/VLE behavioral engagement indicators (login frequency, inactivity, assignment submission)
papers.algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, BLSTM
papers.main_findings: XGBoost achieved the best overall predictive performance. SHAP analysis identified assignment submission regularity, login frequency, learning inactivity, and discussion participation as the most influential predictors. The EWS integrates automated prediction, behavioral visualization, explainable analytics, and personalized intervention recommendations.

papers.title: A Machine Learning-Based Computational System Proposal for Predicting Dropout Events (PDE)
papers.authors: Maria do Carmo Nicoletti, et al.
papers.objective: In the literature related to higher education, the concept of dropout has been approached from several perspectives and, over the years, its definition has been influenced by the use of diversified semantic interpretations. In a general higher education environment dropout can be broadly characterized as the act of a s...
papers.abstract: In the literature related to higher education, the concept of dropout has been approached from several perspectives and, over the years, its definition has been influenced by the use of diversified semantic interpretations. In a general higher education environment dropout can be broadly characterized as the act of a student engaged in a course leaving the educational institution without finishing the course. This paper describes the proposal of the architecture of a computational system, PDE (Predicting Dropout Events), based on machine learning (ML) algorithms and specifically designed for predicting dropout events in a higher level educational environment.
papers.preprocessing: Feature selection (Relief, Focus / RFE-CV); Educational data preprocessing pipeline
papers.algorithms: Instance-Based Learning (IBL), k-NN, IB1-IB5, CNN, RNN, SNN
papers.main_findings: IBL algorithms are suitable for dropout prediction due to their simplicity and ease of implementation. Feature selection algorithms (Relief, Focus) are essential for preprocessing educational data. The PDE system follows three main subsystems: Preprocessing, Learning, and Monitoring/Predicting Dropout.

papers.relevance_type: Directly Related to Student Dropout Prediction

papers.title: Early Warning System for First Semester Student Dropout Using Data Driven Risk Stratification
papers.authors: Nourhan Osama Aliraqi, Ahmed Abou El-Fetouh, Maha Zaghloul, Rasha Hassan Saqr
papers.objective: Student dropout in higher education represents a significant challenge for institutions, learners, and economies alike, resulting in substantial losses of human capital and financial resources. This study presents a machine learning-based early warning system designed to identify students at risk of dropping out follow...
papers.abstract: Student dropout in higher education represents a significant challenge for institutions, learners, and economies alike, resulting in substantial losses of human capital and financial resources. This study presents a machine learning-based early warning system designed to identify students at risk of dropping out following the completion of their first academic semester. Using the Higher Education Predictors of Student Retention dataset, comprising 4,424 student records, a binary classification framework was developed and evaluated across six model configurations-Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, each in default and class-balanced variants-trained under three resampling conditions: original, oversampled, and undersampled data.
papers.dataset: Higher Education Predictors of Student Retention (UCI), 4,424 students
papers.algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM
papers.class_imbalance: Class weighting / balanced variants; Random oversampling; Undersampling
papers.evaluation_metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, AUC, F1-score, ROC, AUC-ROC
papers.main_findings: LightGBM with balanced class weighting and random oversampling achieved 87.1% accuracy, 80.4% precision, 79.2% recall, 79.8% F1-score, and 91.2% AUC-ROC. First-semester academic and demographic data are sufficient to support reliable early dropout identification.

papers.objective: The advent of massive open online courses (MOOCs) has revolutionized education, offering unprecedented access to high-quality learning materials globally. papers.abstract: The advent of massive open online courses (MOOCs) has revolutionized education, offering unprecedented access to high-quality learning materials globally. However, high dropout rates pose significant challenges to realizing the full potential of MOOCs. This study explores machine learning techniques for predicting student dropout in MOOCs, utilizing the open university learning analytics dataset (OULAD). Seven algorithms, including decision tree, random forest, Gaussian naive Bayes, AdaBoost classifier, extra tree classifier, XGBoost classifier, and multilayer perceptron (MLP), are employed to predict student outcomes and dropout probabilities.
papers.algorithms: Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gaussian Naive Bayes, AdaBoost, Extra Trees, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)
papers.main_findings: XGBoost classifier emerged as the top performer, achieving 87% accuracy in pass/fail prediction and 86% accuracy in dropout prediction. SMOTE was used to address class imbalance. Personalized interventions based on individual dropout probabilities were proposed.

papers.journal: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
papers.objective: Student drop-out is one of the most burning issues in STEM higher education, which induces considerable social and economic costs. papers.abstract: Student drop-out is one of the most burning issues in STEM higher education, which induces considerable social and economic costs. Using machine learning tools for the early identification of students at risk of dropping out has gained a lot of interest recently. However, there has been little discussion on dropout prediction using interpretable machine learning (IML) and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) tools. In this work, using the data of a large public Hungarian university, we demonstrate how IML and XAI tools can support educational stakeholders in dropout prediction.

papers.algorithms: CatBoost, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, AdaBoost, NGBoost
papers.xai_techniques: SHAP; LIME; Counterfactual / XAI visualizations (user study)
papers.main_findings: CatBoost achieved AUC of 0.774 and average precision of 0.847. HSGPA, mathematics, and chosen subject were the most important features. SHAP and LIME were used for local explanations. A user study evaluated the interpretability and usefulness of XAI visualizations.

papers.objective: Decreasing student attrition rates is one of the main objectives of most higher education institutions. papers.abstract: Decreasing student attrition rates is one of the main objectives of most higher education institutions. However, to achieve this goal, universities need to accurately identify and focus their efforts on students most likely to quit their studies before they graduate. This has given rise to a need to implement forecasting models to predict which students will eventually drop out. In this paper, we present an early warning system to automatically identify first-semester students at high risk of dropping out. The system is based on a machine learning model trained from historical data on first-semester students.
papers.dataset: Universidad Tecnológica de Pereira, Colombia, 6,617 students (2017-2019)
papers.algorithms: Logistic Regression
papers.main_findings: The system can predict 'at-risk' students with a sensitivity of 61.97%. Key predictors included ASSIST drug test variables (tobacco, cannabis, cocaine, amphetamines), depression level, and learning styles. High-risk accuracy was 62.26%.

papers.abstract: In universities, student dropout is a significant concern as it adversely affects both the students and the educational institutions. Identifying students who are at risk of dropping out early allows for timely interventions and support systems to be implemented, thereby enhancing student retention rates. This study focuses on applying machine learning techniques to analyze student behavior and predict early dropout in university settings. The objective of this research is to develop a machine learning-based predictive model that utilizes student behavioral data to identify potential indicators of early dropout.

In this scenario, technical schools have also suffered from considerable dropout levels, even when considering a still increasing need for professionals in areas associated to computing and engineering. This article applies and evaluates XAI methods to predict students in school dropout situation, considering a database of students from the Federal Institute of Rio Grande do Norte (IFRN), a Brazilian technical school.

papers.abstract: Student dropout remains one of the most persistent challenges in education, affecting institutional performance as well as long-term societal development. This study introduces an AI-based Dropout Prediction and Counselling System (ADPoCS) that combines behavioural, academic and socio-economic factors with machine learning techniques to estimate dropout risk. In addition to prediction, the system integrates a counselling module capable of suggesting personalised academic and mental-health support based on each student's risk profile.

papers.abstract: This paper presents a case study on early dropout prediction using data mining with high school students. The study addresses the challenge of identifying students at risk of dropping out early enough to implement effective interventions. Various data mining techniques are employed to predict dropout based on student characteristics and academic performance.

papers.abstract: This study focused on identifying students at risk of academic dropout in higher education through clustering analysis. The research suggested a three-group solution: (1) students with moderate to high cognitive abilities but deficient learning strategies; (2) students with moderate to high cognitive and learning abilities; (3) students with low cognitive functions and moderate learning ability.

papers.abstract: This research presents the design and evaluation of an early warning system based on an XGBoost classifier, trained exclusively on data collected at the time of student enrollment. papers.abstract: We developed a modular dropout prediction pipeline that couples data preprocessing with multi-model benchmarking and a governance-ready explainability layer. Using 17,883 undergraduate records from a Moroccan higher education institution, we evaluated nine algorithms. The pipeline includes a SHAP-based layer identifying risk and protective factors, surfacing ambiguous and anomalous cases for human review, and offering case-level diagnostics.
papers.dataset: Moroccan higher education institution, 17,883 undergraduate records
papers.algorithms: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, KNN, SVM, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, MLP
papers.evaluation_metrics: AUC, F1, Recall, F1-score, ROC, AUC-ROC
papers.main_findings: XGBoost attained AUC-ROC of 0.993, F1-score of 0.911, and recall of 0.944. SHAP-based layer identified risk factors including administrative deadlines, cumulative GPA, and passed-course counts.
papers.limitations: Not explicitly detailed in the 2-page PDF brief

papers.abstract: This paper systematically reviews machine learning methods and risk factors for student dropout prediction. Random Forest was identified in 61 studies and XGBoost in 34 studies as commonly used algorithms. The review synthesizes existing literature to understand the methodological landscape of dropout prediction.
papers.algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost (Meta-Analysis)
papers.main_findings: Random Forest used in 61 studies, XGBoost in 34 studies. Most published studies lack an implemented real-time early warning system and have limited integration of explainability with actionable student interventions.
papers.limitations: Lack of operational real-time EWS and limited integration of XAI with actionable counselor interventions
papers.research_gaps: Need for integrated real-time EWS combining calibrated dropout prediction, standardized XAI, and actionable educator interventions

papers.eduguard_relevance: EduGuard resolves the systematic review gaps by providing an end-to-end deployed EWS with XAI and actionable intervention dossiers.

papers.abstract: This study explores applying Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques to predict student performance in educational settings. This research employs XAI techniques such as SHAP and LIME to explain the predictions. Students' performance scores, such as quizzes, midterm examinations, practical tests, assignments, and activities were used as features to predict the final grades using the Random Forest Classifier (RFC).
papers.dataset: Omani higher education institution student performance dataset
papers.algorithms: Random Forest Classifier with SHAP and LIME
papers.main_findings: The model achieved 92% accuracy and weighted F1-score of 0.90. Midterm marks, quiz scores, and assignments are critical features. Limitations include scalability issues with large data for LIME, bias/fairness challenges, and lack of standardized interpretability metrics.
papers.limitations: LIME scalability issues on large datasets, bias/fairness challenges, lack of standardized interpretability metrics

papers.relevance_type: Related Educational ML & Explainability (Grade Prediction / Academic Success)
papers.eduguard_relevance: Dual SHAP-LIME explanatory verification, Partial Dependence analysis, and student-level interactive breakdowns.

papers.abstract: Machine Learning concept learns from experiences, inferences and conceives complex queries. Machine learning techniques can be used to develop the educational framework which understands the inputs from students, parents and with intelligence generates the result. The framework integrates the features of Machine Learning (ML), Explainable AI (XAI) to analyze the educational factors which are helpful to students in achieving career placements.

papers.limitations: Small dataset (215 instances) focused on placement rather than dropout
